text:
maria (platform): Heads-up — found a customer case where a retry after a socket timeout caused two billable token deductions. They retried a generation, backend returned 5xx during streaming, but the server actually completed and charged. We need a clear strategy to prevent double-charging on retries.

josh (api): Oof. Do we have an idempotency key requirement on text/generate? I thought only bulk/async endpoints had it.

liam (billing): We currently decrement token balance as soon as a request is accepted by the serving runtime. That makes accounting simple but is vulnerable to duplicate requests.

maria (platform): Right. Options I see: 1) require X-Idempotency-Key for any mutating call and dedupe in the gateway; 2) do a reserve-with-ttl (hold tokens) then finalize on success/rollback on failure; 3) make billing eventually consistent and run dedupe post-hoc with credits. Thoughts on tradeoffs?

eva (sre): 1) is easiest UX-wise but hard to enforce for existing clients. 2) adds complexity but prevents user-visible double-charges. 3) has customer-experience risk (manual credits). Also consider retries at network layer vs client-sent duplicate keys. Telemetry needs to surface all three.

josh (api): We should support idempotency header but not require it immediately. For unknown requests, fall back to reserve flow. Proposed default flow: gateway tries idempotency lookup -> if hit, short-circuit and return cached response; if miss, atomically reserve tokens + forward -> on success finalize and store idempotency key -> on failure release reservation.

liam (billing): That sounds good. Important: reserve operations must be atomic with respect to quota counters, else we still race on bursts. We should use a single Redis Lua script or DB transaction that checks remaining_quota >= reserve_amount, subtracts reserve_amount, and sets a reservation key with TTL.

nora (product): For the console, we'd want a new dashboard tile: "reserved tokens" vs "committed tokens" and a timeline for idempotency hits/misses. Also a table for "rollback_count" per-org so CSMs can spot noise.

quota-bot: metric emitted: quota.reserve.success, quota.reserve.fail, quota.commit, quota.rollback, idempotency.hit, idempotency.miss

maria (platform): Example Lua sketch (very rough):
```
-- KEYS[1] = org_quota_key
-- KEYS[2] = reservation_key (org:res:<idempotency>)
-- ARGV[1] = reserve_amount
-- ARGV[2] = reservation_ttl
local q = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) or '0')
if q >= tonumber(ARGV[1]) then
  redis.call('DECRBY', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
  redis.call('SET', KEYS[2], ARGV[1], 'PX', ARGV[2])
  return 1
else
  return 0
end
```

josh (api): Nice. A few gotchas: streaming responses may produce tokens incrementally. If client disconnects and retries with same idempotency key, we need to be able to attach the new connection to the same in-flight session or replay only missing tokens. Maybe reserve full worst-case or reserve in windows (e.g., per-chunk).

eva (sre): For streaming, we should reserve an initial envelope (e.g., 32 tokens) and then do incremental commit as chunks are produced. That avoids large upfront reservations while still protecting against quick dupes. Also eviction TTL should cover our client retry window (default ~60s).

liam (billing): We must be careful about refunds: if reservation expired (TTL) but server later commits, we could undercount. So reservation finalization must delete the reservation key atomically and increment committed usage elsewhere. The finalize step must succeed or we trigger an operational alert.

maria (platform): Agreed. We'll implement finalize as: check reservation key exists and equals expected -> atomically move reserved -> add to committed counter and delete reservation key -> write idempotency entry with reference to finalizing request and response checksum. If finalize fails, we log and retry with exponential backoff; if retrying risks double-commit, use compare-and-swap via idempotency entry.

josh (api): Edge-case: clients that don't set idempotency key but retry after a network issue. For them the reserve path still helps, but duplicates can still happen if two retries occur before reservation TTL expires. We should document best practices: set idempotency key, exponential backoff, and don't re-use keys across different prompts.

nora (product): UX ask: make the gateway response for a deduped request include a header `X-Idempotency-Status: replay|cached|new` so integrators know what happened. Also surface a small timeline in logs in Console.

eva (sre): Telemetry we need: per-org gauge reserved_tokens, counter idempotency_replays, histogram retry_latency, counter double_charge_attempts. Alert: if double_charge_attempts > 0 for more than 1hr for any org -> page SRE + billing.

liam (billing): On billing semantics: customers expect not to be charged twice. We should consider automatic credits when we detect a duplicate finalization within a short window and show a credit event in billing history. But prefer prevention over cure.

maria (platform): Action items: 1) API: add optional `X-Idempotency-Key` support + `X-Idempotency-Status` header (josh) 2) Runtime: implement reserve+finalize Lua flow and streaming incremental commits (eva + eng-runtime) 3) Billing: add committed/reserved counters, credits handling, and runbook for rollback (liam) 4) Console: new panels for reservation vs committed + dedupe table (nora) 5) Telemetry: add metrics from quota-bot (maria)

josh (api): I'll open a RFC with the header spec and example client flows. I'll include sample error codes: 429.reserve_failed, 409.duplicate_commit, 202.queued_when_reserving

eva (sre): Also add a circuit-breaker when reservation fail-rate is high for an org -> route to degraded path (lower qps) and show in Console.

maria (platform): One more subtlety — idempotency cache growth. We need eviction policy and size limits per-org. Recommendation: store idempotency entries with TTL of 7 days for billing disputes, but keep quick lookup cache for 24h hot window. Paging older entries to cold storage for audits.

liam (billing): Sounds good. For auditability, log raw request checksum + response checksum and store in cold storage. That will let us prove duplicate responses if customers dispute charges.

nora (product): I'll mock the console panels and add a tooltip that explains why reserved != committed. Also add CTA to docs: "how to avoid double charges".

maria (platform): Thanks all. I'll coordinate RFC + small spike for Lua script and metric plumbing. If anyone wants to pair on the streaming commit design, ping me. :pray:
